basketball team|Team competition]]}} }} '''Shelden DeMar Williams''' (born October 21, 1983) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. Nicknamed "'''the Landlord'''",[https://web.archive.org/web/20031004110936/http://www.nbadraft.net/profiles/sheldenwilliams.asp NBA Draft.net profile] he played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], and later played in the NBA for parts of seven seasons. Williams earned the 2005 and 2006 [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year]] Awards while at Duke, becoming only the fifth player in history to earn the award two consecutive years. He holds Duke's career blocks record, single-season blocks record, and career rebounding record. ==High school career== During high school, Williams was a member of the [[National Honor Society]] and the [[Fellowship of Christian Athletes]]. *2002 EA Sports High School All-America selection *Gatorade Oklahoma Player of the Year: 2001, 2002 *2001 USA Today Oklahoma Player of the Year *Oklahoma Player of the Year in 2001 by the Daily Oklahoman *Oklahoma Defensive Player of the Year: 2000, 2001 *Ranked number 49 in the nation among all players by ESPN.com following his senior season (averaging 20 points, 12 rebounds, three blocked shots and three assists as a senior) *Rated the nation's fifth-best prep player by Future Stars and BlueChipHoops.com and sixth by College Basketball News entering the 2001–02 season *The Sporting News listed Williams as the nation's sixth-best prep player entering 2001–02 *Rated the nation's number one forward by Basketball News and [[Prepstar]] *Three-time all-state, all-district and all-city selection (1999–2001) *2001 Parade All-America ==College career== Williams played for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke University men's basketball team]] from 2002 to 2006. He majored in [[sociology]] with a markets and management studies certificate. Williams became only the third Duke basketball player{{Cite web |url=http://www.clutchfans.net/nbadraft/profiles/2006/shelden_williams/ |title=Shelden Williams NBA Draft Profile |access-date=June 1, 2006 |archive-date=January 25, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125172945/https://clutchfans.net/nbadraft/profiles/2006/shelden_williams/ |url-status=dead }} to record a [[triple-double]] when Duke defeated Maryland on January 11, 2006, recording 19 points, 11 rebounds and 10 blocks.[https://web.archive.org/web/20170314152808/http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=260110150 Williams' triple-double leads Duke to blowout win over MD] On January 28, 2007, Duke retired Williams' No. 23 jersey. Williams is the third player in [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] history to have 1,500 [[point (basketball)|points]], 1,000 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], 350 blocks and 150 steals (joining [[Tim Duncan]] and [[Ralph Sampson]]). His 1,217 rebounds and 1,859 career points rank him seventh in ACC history and sixteenth in Duke history, respectively. ===Records=== As of graduating from Duke University, Williams held records for: *Duke all-time leader in blocked shots (422) *Duke all-time leader in rebounds *Duke single season blocked shots ===Awards=== * [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] [[NABC Defensive Player of the Year|Defensive Player of the Year]]: 2005, 2006 * [[Associated Press]] First Team All American: 2006 * [[John R. Wooden Award|John R. Wooden]] First Team All American: 2006 *Senior CLASS All-Senior All American Team: 2006 *John R. Wooden National Player of the Year Finalist: 2006 *NBA Rookie of the Month: April 2007 ==Professional career== ===Atlanta Hawks (2006–2008)=== Williams was selected by the [[Atlanta Hawks]] with the fifth overall pick in the [[2006 NBA draft]]. On July 10, 2006, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Hawks.{{Cite web |title=Hawks Sign Shelden Williams |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/Hawks_Sign_Shelden_Williams_071006.html |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=Atlanta Hawks}} On November 1, Williams made his NBA debut, recording three rebounds and one block in a 75–88 loss to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks vs Philadelphia 76ers Nov 1, 2006 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020600003 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=NBA}} On April 16, 2007, he logged a season-high 17 rebounds, alongside 16 points, in a 96–102 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Hawks vs Milwaukee Bucks Apr 16, 2007 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020601205 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=NBA}} A day later, he scored a season-high 21 points, alongside ten rebounds, in a 118–102 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=Indiana Pacers vs Atlanta Hawks Apr 17, 2007 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020601213 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=NBA}} Williams was named the NBA Eastern Conference Rookie of the Month for games played in April.{{Cite web |title=NBA Rookies of the Month |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/rom.html |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=Basketball Reference}} ===Sacramento Kings (2008–2009)=== On February 16, 2008, Williams was traded, alongside [[Anthony Johnson (basketball)|Anthony Johnson]], [[Tyronn Lue]], [[Lorenzen Wright]] and a 2008 second-round pick, to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Mike Bibby]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3249180] Kings sending guard Bibby to Hawks for four players On April 15, Williams logged a season-high 11 rebounds, alongside 12 points and three steals, in a 101–124 loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{Cite web |title=Sacramento Kings vs Los Angeles Lakers Apr 15, 2008 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0020701216 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |website=NBA}} He averaged 0.7 points per game. ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2009)=== On February 19, 2009, Williams was traded, alongside [[Bobby Brown (basketball)|Bobby Brown]], to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] in exchange for [[Rashad McCants]] and [[Calvin Booth]].{{cite press release |title = KINGS ACQUIRE RASHAD McCANTS AND CALVIN BOOTH |publisher = Sacramento Kings |date = February 19, 2009 |url = http://www.nba.com/kings/news/Press_Release_021909.html |access-date = February 20, 2009}} ===Boston Celtics married former [[University of Tennessee]] [[Tennessee Lady Volunteers basketball|Lady Vols]] and [[Las Vegas Aces]] basketball star [[Candace Parker]]. They have a daughter named Lailaa. In November 2016, Williams filed for divorce claiming irreconcilable differences. They had been living separately for 3 months prior to the divorce. They share joint custody with neither paying child support to the other. Shelden started the Shelden Williams Foundation in 2019. The Shelden Williams Foundation is dedicated to empowering student athletes and their families by delivering and supporting initiatives that promote emotional and physical health through sports,
